title: Gene, allele, genotype, phenotype
examples: What is the difference between genotype and phenotype?
Can you give me an example of a dominant allele?
How do I know if I am homozygous or heterozygous?

explain.say: Today we are learning about genes and traits. A gene is a section of DNA that gives instructions for a trait.

draw.text: Gene: DNA segment for a trait

explain.say: An allele is a specific version of a gene. Think of it like different colors for the same trait.
Genotype shows the combination of alleles you have. It is the actual genetic makeup you inherit.
Phenotype is the physical trait you actually see. It is the result of your genes and environment.
Dominant alleles show their trait even if only one copy is present. They mask the other allele's effect.
Recessive alleles only show their trait if two copies are present. They need a partner allele to be hidden.

faq.q: What is the difference between genotype and phenotype?
faq.a: The genotype is your genetic code, the combination of alleles you carry. The phenotype is what you actually look like because of those genes.
asks: What is the difference between genes and traits?
Is genotype what I see or what I have?

faq.q: How do I know if an allele is dominant or recessive?
faq.a: We determine this by observing which trait appears when both alleles are present. The dominant allele's trait will be visible.

faq.q: What does it mean to be heterozygous?
faq.a: Heterozygous means you have two different alleles for a gene, like one dominant and one recessive. For example, Bb.
asks: What is the opposite of heterozygous?
If I have two different alleles, what is that called?

faq.a: Homozygous means you have two identical alleles for a gene. You could have two dominant or two recessive alleles.
asks: Do I have to have the same alleles to be homozygous?
What are the two types of homozygous?

faq.q: Can the environment change my phenotype?
faq.a: Yes, the environment can affect your phenotype. For example, diet can affect your height, even if your genes are set.
asks: Are genes the only thing that determines traits?
How much does environment affect biology?

facts: Genes are segments of DNA located on chromosomes.
Alleles determine specific versions of a gene, such as different eye colors.
If an allele is dominant, its trait will show even with one copy.
An individual with two different alleles is called heterozygous.
The physical expression of genes is called the phenotype.

quiz.say: A person has the genotype Bb for a trait. If B is dominant, what is their phenotype?
quiz.show: Genotype Bb, B is dominant. Phenotype?

options.show: The trait will be a mix of B and b.
options.say: The trait will be a mix of B and b.

options.show: The trait will only show if both are present.
options.say: The trait will only show if both are present.

quiz.why: Because B is dominant, its trait will show, even though the person also has the recessive allele b.

wrong.1: This is tempting because it suggests blending, but traits are usually distinct, not mixed.
wrong.2: This is wrong because the dominant allele always masks the recessive one.
wrong.3: This confuses the requirement for recessiveness with the presence of a dominant allele.

quiz.say: If an individual is homozygous recessive for a trait, what does this mean?

options.show: It means the person has no genes for that trait.
options.say: It means the person has no genes for that trait.

options.show: The trait will only show if both alleles are recessive.
options.say: The trait will only show if both alleles are recessive.

quiz.why: To be homozygous recessive, you must have two copies of the recessive allele, allowing the trait to be expressed.

wrong.0: This assumes the trait cannot be seen, but it is expressed when two recessive alleles are present.
wrong.1: This is incorrect because the alleles are present, just both are recessive.
wrong.2: This confuses the state of the alleles with the expression of the trait.

quiz.say: Which term describes the physical appearance, like eye color?
quiz.why: Phenotype refers to the observable physical trait, which is what you can see or measure.

wrong.0: Homozygous describes the pairing of alleles, not the observable trait.
wrong.2: Genotype is the underlying genetic code, not the visible trait itself.
wrong.3: An allele is just one version of a gene, not the overall physical outcome.
